output.myth: Ennu the Kite-Wright carved a gull from whalebone, the winter the boats stayed on the shingle. He gave it goat-hide wings and tied its string to Hesk's reel. Go and find the drowned, he told it, and bring me their names. The gull went out over the cold water and came back each night with a name in its beak, and Hesk wound each one onto the reel and kept count. Nobody ever asked how many. Then Aun, who cannot leave a string alone, climbed the cliff with his knife to see what the gull was for. He cut the string. The gull did not fall. It rose, and it is still rising, past the Far Wing and the Trailing Lamp, carrying the names it has not yet delivered. When the wind is from the north you can see it there. If you are the counting sort, do not try. You will lose your place and have to start again.
output.verse:
Ennu cut the bone
and Hesk counted every string
the gull still flies home
